topStories.headline: SFSU's Student Center Awaits a New Name as Renaming Panel Nears Its Deadline
topStories.dek: After two days of town halls, Associated Students must deliver a renaming recommendation to its Board of Directors by the end of October.
topStories.body:
San Francisco State University's central student building has been without an official name since 2026, when sexual-abuse allegations against Cesar Chavez — after whom the building had been named since the 1970s — prompted the university's student government to begin a renaming process. The building, which opened in 1975 and houses a 500-seat auditorium, student lounges, dining, and offices for dozens of student organizations, currently has its signage covered.

Associated Students wrapped up its two-day town hall series on October 7, hearing from students, faculty, staff, and alumni about potential new names. Among the loudest voices at the final session were members of the League of Filipino Students, who advocated naming the center after Lyle Prijoles, a Filipino-American SFSU alumnus and activist.

The Ad Hoc Committee tasked with the decision is working toward a recommendation to the AS Board of Directors by the end of October. From there, both university President Lynn Mahoney and the California State University Board of Trustees must ratify the new name before the spring 2027 semester begins.

Three naming themes emerged earlier in the process from a community survey: the Farmworkers Movement, the 1968 Third World Liberation Front Strike, and the 1969 occupation of Alcatraz. Individual name suggestions were also collected. The committee has not yet publicly indicated which direction it is leaning.

topStories.headline: Sbarro Is Coming Back to Stonestown — After a Four-Year Absence
topStories.dek: The mall-food-court pizza chain is set to reclaim the upper-level space it vacated in 2022, replacing Bay Area chain Blondie's Pizza, which left owing back rent.
topStories.body:
Stonestown Galleria confirmed this week that Sbarro will return to its food court, expected sometime in the first quarter of 2027. The chain will occupy the same upper-level spot it held before Blondie's Pizza took over the space roughly four years ago.

Blondie's had signed a decade-long lease when it moved in, but Stonestown's operator sued the restaurant in January, alleging it owed more than $74,000 in unpaid rent. After a default notice and a pay-or-vacate notice, Blondie's vacated the space, clearing the way for the Brooklyn-founded, Ohio-headquartered chain to return.

Sbarro will join Blaze Pizza as the mall's second pizzeria. The return announcement drew a wave of nostalgia on social media, with a Reddit thread drawing hundreds of upvotes from commenters who remembered eating there as children.

The news continues a busy stretch for Stonestown. Raising Cane's opened its second San Francisco location at the mall earlier this month, drawing more than 200 people to its grand opening, with some fans camping overnight. Chinese boba tea chain Chagee is also expected to open in the food court in early 2027.

topStories.headline: West Portal Tower Grows Again: Empire Theater Site Now Proposed at 13 Stories, 172 Units
topStories.dek: Developers have responded to community pushback by adding floors and units — not removing them — in a project that would dwarf everything else on the West Portal Avenue corridor.
topStories.body:
A proposed housing development on the site of the shuttered Empire Theater at 85 West Portal Avenue has grown yet again, now reaching 13 stories and 172 units — nearly three times the 64-unit, nine-story building that debuted in January. The latest update to the project was reported this week by the Sunset Beacon.

Developer DM Development, acting for Empire West Portal LLC, expanded the project after acquiring an adjacent parcel at 59 West Portal Avenue, currently occupied by Goodwill and Supercuts, and by stacking Mayor Daniel Lurie's Family Zoning changes with two state housing laws — SB-330 and AB-2011 — that together roughly double allowable density and enable a streamlined, over-the-counter approval that bypasses the lengthy public-hearing process.

The revised plans call for 21 studios, 52 one-bedrooms, 72 two-bedrooms, and 27 three-bedrooms, with 26 units deed-restricted as affordable housing — half for very low-income households and half for moderate-income families. The ground floor would include approximately 7,000 square feet of retail, and 89 underground parking spaces would be provided. Handel Architects is the designer of record.

The building, at roughly 156 feet, would be the tallest structure on a commercial corridor where almost nothing exceeds three or four stories. DM Development has not released a construction timeline. Local merchants have expressed anxiety about disruption to the avenue during what could be a multi-year build.

moreNews.headline: Miraloma Park Improvement Club Hosts Congressional Candidate Forum This Fall
moreNews.body: The Miraloma Park Improvement Club's October 2026 newsletter, published this month, invites residents to a congressional candidate forum being organized by the club. The newsletter, distributed to the neighborhood's roughly 2,200 households, also highlights October as earthquake preparedness month and includes a feature on reducing home fire risk. The MPIC holds its regular monthly meetings on the first Thursday of each month at 7 PM at the MPIC Clubhouse, 350 O'Shaughnessy Boulevard. No specific date for the candidate forum was listed in publicly available materials; residents should check miralomapark.org for updates.

moreNews.headline: City Seeks Private Partner to Redevelop Former Lake Merced Gun Range Into Public Park
moreNews.body: San Francisco Recreation and Park Department launched a request for proposals in summer 2026 to find a private operator to build and run a new public park on the roughly 10-acre former Pacific Rod and Gun Club site on the west shore of Lake Merced (520 John Muir Drive). The site completed lead and asbestos remediation in 2025. A community meeting was held at the Lake Merced Boathouse on July 30, 2026, at which Rec and Park presented the RFP and outlined possible amenities — including a boathouse, restaurant, dock, trails, and recreation courts. Proposal submissions were expected through August and September 2026, with final approval required from the Recreation and Park Commission and the Board of Supervisors. No selection has been publicly announced as of this writing.
